b: I'm a book slogger. I'll battle through something I start till I finish it. Usually, through the journey I get some redemption through theme, insight, surprise, nuance, etc.

Ayn Rand's fictional treatise on her Objectivist philosophy is so comically one note that a couple hundred pages in, you get it. Reading it today, the hero industrialists who make things and therefore keep society functioning through their genius falls so flat when we think about runaway capitalism exploiting people and resources. These good guys are one note caricatures. The bad guys- any person with a humanist concern- are caricatures.
It's a such a simple book. And it's so effusive and self important. I reckon that is by design since; according to Rand, it was the purest distillation of her philosophy.

One might say that only our modern lens would demand wrestling with privilege, power, misogyny, worker exploitation, social welfare, etc. And so there might be a reason to forgive the book's grossly simple terms. It was after all a different time and new industry and tech was booming. But good literature, regardless of when it is written, opens doors for some such discussions- especially if you're trying to justify a new philosophy set against all that has come before.
